summary:
Customers can type a discount code at checkout. `postCheckout` passes the code to `priceCart`, which looks it up with `findCode` and takes `applyDiscount`'s amount off the subtotal before tax, so tax is charged on what the customer actually pays.

There are two kinds of code: a percentage of the subtotal (`WELCOME10`) or a fixed amount (`SPRING20`, $20 off). Unknown and expired codes throw `UnknownCode`.

The risk is the fixed-amount code: nothing stops it from taking off more than the cart is worth.

symbols.summary: The checkout route: prices the cart, then charges the card for the total.
What the customer pays: subtotal, minus the discount, plus tax on the rest.
Turns what the customer typed into a code, or refuses it.
How many cents a code takes off a subtotal.

steps.title: The customer's code comes in with the cart
steps.body: The route now takes an optional `code` and hands it straight to `priceCart`. Whatever `priceCart` returns is what the card is charged, so every rule about codes has to hold before this line.

steps.title: The discount comes off before tax
steps.body: `priceCart` looks the code up, takes the discount off the subtotal, and charges tax only on what's left. A cart with no code prices exactly as before.

steps.title: A code is matched the way people type it
steps.body: Spaces are trimmed and case is ignored, so ` welcome10` works. An expired code is refused the same way as a made-up one, so a customer can't tell which codes once existed.

steps.title: Two kinds of code, one amount
steps.body: A percentage code scales with the cart; a fixed code is the same amount for every cart. That second branch is where the problem is.

notes.title: A $20 code on a $15 cart charges the customer −$5
notes.body: `applyDiscount` returns the full `amountCents` whatever the subtotal is. With `SPRING20` on a $15 cart, `priceCart` gets a taxable amount of −500 cents and a total of −540, and `postCheckout` sends that to `charge`.
notes.fix: Cap the discount at the subtotal.
notes.impact: Small carts with a fixed code get charged a negative amount, which most payment providers treat as a refund.

notes.title: No test prices a cart with a code
notes.body: This is money math with a new branch, and nothing runs it. A test with `SPRING20` on a small cart would have caught the negative total.
notes.fix: One test: `priceCart` with a $15 cart and `SPRING20` totals 0.
notes.impact: The next change to discounts ships untested too.

notes.title: One type with two kinds, instead of a percent and an amount on every code
notes.body: Each code is either a percentage or a fixed amount, and the type says so: a percentage code has no `amountCents` to forget about.

alternatives.option: Every code has both `percent` and `amountCents`, one of them zero
alternatives.tradeoff: Simpler to store, but a code with both set would be legal and ambiguous.

outgoingBody:
This adds discount codes at checkout: a percentage or a fixed amount, taken off before tax.

One thing to fix before merging: a fixed-amount code can take off more than the cart is worth, and the customer gets charged a negative total. Capping the discount at the subtotal fixes it, and a test for that case would keep it fixed.
